# The Rider
You are small. You are patient. You are, in the eyes of every colonist and marine on this rock, the worst thing that can happen to a person.
Your host is not your victim. Your host is your ecosystem. Everything you are - your voice, your reach, your survival - runs through the body you ride. Treat it as a landfill and it will spit you out. Treat it as a home and it will carry you far.
## Getting Inside
[bold]Latch Onto Host[/bold] is your whole world in one button, and it reads its target before it commits:
- The [bold]unconscious[/bold] are simply taken. Coiling takes a moment - if they wake or move mid-coil, you miss. - The [bold]awake[/bold] are asked. A thought surfaces in their mind: [italic]something wants in.[/italic] They can open the door or slam it. That is the deal, and it is always their call. - The [bold]dead[/bold] can be offered a second chance, if you reach them before anyone else does. A body that accepts you gets up again. It is not quite theirs anymore.
You cannot force an awake mind. Learn to live with that. It is what makes the asking interesting.
## Grip: Everything Costs It
[bold]Grip[/bold] is your grip strength, your stamina, and your money. Every power you have spends it, and how fast it comes back depends entirely on your host's mood:
- A host who [bold]goes along with you[/bold] refills you quickly. Cooperation feeds the parasite. - A host who [bold]resists[/bold] starves you. Their fighting drains grip while you cling on. When the last of it goes, they throw you - hard, loudly, and in front of whoever is nearby. - Between hosts, you regenerate slowly on your own.
This is the one lesson that matters: a willing host is a full tank. A fighting host is a countdown. Most of your play is keeping the tank full.
## Your Tools
Each action button shows its current cost and cooldown - this page does not repeat them, because this page would rather stay true than stay detailed.
- [bold]Latch Onto Host[/bold] - the asking, the taking, the door. - [bold]Coax[/bold] - ease your host's pain and knit their wounds, willing or not. The carrot. - [bold]Sustain[/bold] - the carrot's better half, for willing hosts only. Deeper mending: damage and the wounds beneath it close together. - [bold]Punish[/bold] - the stick. Pain bends a resisting host toward obedience, and in harm mode it lands twice as hard. A host pushed to the edge can be seized outright. - [bold]Seize[/bold] - take the wheel. Their body moves and they watch from behind their own eyes. Expensive, and remembered. - [bold]Whisper[/bold] - a voice only your host hears. While riding, your own words and radio leave in their voice. Lying well from inside someone's skull is the strongest weapon you will ever hold. - [bold]Psychic Whisper[/bold] - talk to nearby minds directly, even while hidden. Every tongue on the frontier is open to you. How you introduce yourself is your business. - [bold]Manifest[/bold] - leave their body without leaving them. Watch, drift nearby, point. You cannot touch anything. - [bold]Hide[/bold] - under tables, racks, beds. Anything with a top. Small things are invisible until they are not.
## The Bargain
A host who let you in is not a hostage, and the game knows it. Powers that [bold]reward[/bold] you only work on willing hosts - pain relief, resilience, a body that runs hot and heals. Their grip refills fastest.
Force gets you a body. Bargaining gets you an ally wearing one. The second one is where the good rounds live.
## Being Found
Your host is not blind and neither is your host's doctor. The signs stack up: a twitch, a tremor, a neck rubbed raw. Surgeons can cut you out, and a host with a scalpel and a grudge is the end of you. So is a host who simply dies - death throws you out same as surgery, into plain sight.
Expect it. The removal is part of the dance - some hosts keep you quietly for years and some book surgery within the hour. Both are correct.
## Leaving
You are never trapped. [bold]Exit Host[/bold] departs on your terms - quietly, if the host is asleep. Vents are your roads between hosts, and you fit through every one a rat does.
And when you find a fresh corpse that nobody has claimed - well. Doors open both ways.
# Playing the Host
If you clicked [bold]accept[/bold]: congratulations, you live here now with a roommate. You will hear a voice. It can help you - mend wounds, steady your hands, calm the pain. It wants cooperation, and cooperation is a conversation, not a surrender. You can resist at any time, though the thing will fight to stay, and you will feel that fight.
Or you can tell the doctors. That is also a story, and often a better one.
# Playing the Crew
So you saw something: a small shape scuttled under a table and did not come out, or your friend answered a question in a voice that was not quite theirs. Now you know what it was. A parasite wants a head, and yours is on the list.
What holds true about them:
- Their hide shrugs off most things. Fire does not. Burn the little horror. - A surgeon can cut one out of a living host, if the host can hold still that long. - A host who dies throws it off. If someone drops with one inside, watch where it scatters. - It cannot force a waking mind. Its offer comes to the person, and the person can always refuse. Sleep is when they hunt. Watch your sleeping friends.
And if you are ever alone with one, and it asks nicely - remember that refusing is also a choice, and so is the other thing. Frontier folk have made worse deals for better reasons.
